how.title: Planned like a real show
how.lead: Real drone shows are choreographed before take-off. Skyloom does the same three jobs in your browser.

design.title: Design
design.body: Shapes, words, 3D models and your own pictures are sampled into evenly spaced points — one per drone, coloured from the source.

animate.title: Animate
animate.body: Each drone is assigned the nearest free point, routes are checked for conflicts, and timing is stretched until nobody exceeds the fleet's top speed.

share.title: Share
share.body: The whole show fits in a link. Send it, export a video, or save it as a preset and keep editing.

Landing.exploreHint: Drag to look around · scroll or pinch to zoom · Esc to exit

features.title: Anything you can draw, the fleet can build
features.lead: Every formation is made the same way: your idea becomes evenly spaced points, one per drone, and the fleet flies to them.

text.title: Words in any script
text.body: Type English, 日本語, 中文 or မြန်မာ and press Enter. Latin letters get depth; dense scripts fly as a flat, readable sign.

shapes.title: Eighteen ready shapes
shapes.body: Heart, galaxy, DNA helix, Saturn, butterfly and more. Solid shapes turn slowly so you can see their depth.

artwork.title: Your pictures and SVG
artwork.body: Drop a photo, logo or line icon. Drones take its outline and its colours.

models.title: 3D models that move
models.body: Link a .glb from your device. If it has animation, play it as a run of formations the fleet flies through.

physics.title: Real flight limits
physics.body: Top speed, acceleration and a safety gap are enforced. Routes are planned before take-off so no two drones meet.

share.title: Share and export
share.body: A whole show fits in a link. Save presets, export stills and video, and keep editing.

guide.title: Your first show in a minute
guide.lead: Everything happens in the panel beside the show. No account, nothing to install.

pick.title: Pick a show
pick.body: Open the Show tab and choose one. The drones already in the air re-form into it.

create.title: Add your own formation
create.body: In Create, type a word, pick a shape or drop a file. It joins the show and the fleet flies straight to it.

look.title: Set the look
look.body: Look changes drone size, lighting and colours; Flight sets speed and spacing. Every group has its own reset.

explore.title: Step inside
explore.body: Explore in 3D lets you orbit and zoom, or walk under the show. Open the Studio for a timeline and export.

files.a: Nowhere. Pictures, SVG and models are read in your browser and never uploaded. Large files stay on your device and are only linked; if one is moved, you are asked to locate it.

saved.a: Yes, automatically on this device. Reset any group of settings, or everything, whenever you like.

devices.a: Any recent browser. WebGPU is used where available, with a WebGL fallback. The fleet size adapts to what your device can fly smoothly.

real.q: Could a real fleet fly this?
real.a: The planning follows the same rules: speed and acceleration limits, a minimum gap and conflict-free routes. It is a design tool, not flight software.

library.title: 1 · Add formations
library.body: Pick a shape or 3D model, type a word, or upload a picture. Each one is added to your show and the drones fly into it.

timeline.title: 2 · Arrange the show
timeline.body: Formations play left to right. Click a card to fly there, drag to reorder, and use the buttons on a card to duplicate or delete it.

inspector.title: 3 · Shape and style
inspector.body: The first tab edits the selected formation. The others change the whole show: drones, flight rules, scene, camera and effects.

share.title: 4 · Save and share
share.body: Your work saves automatically. Use Shows to load or save presets, Share to copy a link, and Export for a picture or video. Undo is always there.

meta.title: Guide
meta.description: How to design, fly and share a drone show with Skyloom.

Guide.title: Fly your first show
Guide.lead: Everything happens live: change something and the fleet re-forms in front of you.

pick.title: Pick a show
pick.body: Choose a show from the gallery or the Show tab. The drones already in the air fly straight into it.

create.title: Add formations
create.body: Type a shape or a word, tap a shape, or upload a picture, SVG or .glb model. Text can be English, Japanese or Burmese.

look.title: Make it yours
look.body: Set drone size, LED size and glow, pick one colour, a rainbow or random colours, and dim the background until the lights stand out.

flight.title: Set the rules of flight
flight.body: Choose the fleet size, the top speed in metres per second and the minimum gap between drones. Flight times stretch to obey them.

views.title: Watch from anywhere
views.body: Stand in the crowd, zoom in to see the propellers, or switch to Walk and stroll under the show with W A S D or the arrow keys.

studio.title: Go deeper in the studio
studio.body: The studio adds a timeline, per-formation timing and spin, camera shots, physics moments, undo and redo.

share.title: Share and export
share.body: Copy a link that contains the whole show, save a PNG, or render a video frame by frame.

meta.title: About
meta.description: How Skyloom plans a drone show: sampling, assignment, collision-free routes and real flight speeds.

About.title: How the show is planned
About.lead: Skyloom is a simulator. It borrows the steps a real show goes through before a single drone leaves the ground.

sampling.title: Shapes become points
sampling.body: Meshes, text, pictures and 3D models are sampled into one point per drone, then pushed apart until every drone has a safety gap around it.

assignment.title: Every drone gets a target
assignment.body: Drones and targets are sorted along a space-filling curve and paired, then swapped wherever a swap shortens the trip. Short trips rarely cross.

routes.title: Routes are checked before take-off
routes.body: Each transition is sampled in time. Any two drones that would pass too close get their routes bent apart, and the check repeats until it is clean.

speed.title: Time follows speed
speed.body: A transition lasts as long as the farthest-flying drone needs at the fleet's top speed. Lower the speed limit and the show slows down, like a real one.

rendering.title: One draw call for the fleet
rendering.body: Positions are computed on the GPU and every drone is drawn in a single instanced call: an LED sprite plus a small quadcopter with spinning propellers.

limits.title: What it is not
limits.body: Drones are drawn larger than life so you can see them, wind and battery are not modelled, and nothing here is a flight plan for real aircraft.

About.disclaimer: Virtual simulation only. Bundled 3D models and typefaces come from the three.js examples (MIT licence).
